 5 Big Changes From November 1, 2026: From Delhi Pollution Rules To New Banking Fees, Check List Of Things To Keep In Mind Ahead Of The New Month
 By Aishwarya Samant Last Updated: Oct 26, 2026, 14:35 IST November 1, 2026, may bring important changes affecting commuters, train passengers, bank customers and pensioners. From Delhi's winter pollution measures to railway booking rules, telecom regulations, banking fees and Digital Life Certificates, here are five key updates to watch.
 5 Big Changes From November 1, 2026: From Delhi Pollution Rules To New Banking Fees, Check List Of Things To Keep In Mind Ahead Of The New Month
 5 Big Changes From 1 November, 2026: As always, the new month will mark the official beginning of winter. The winter season will bring many changes for day-to-day consumers. 
 With the biggest festive season approaching and temperatures gradually dropping, citizens will need to keep an eye on important regulatory and administrative changes. 
 From pollution-control measures in Delhi to railway ticket booking rules, banking charges and telecom regulations, these developments could affect everyday travel, digital payments and financial planning. Pensioners will also enter the annual period for submitting their Digital Life Certificates. These changes apply to everyone, irrespective of age and region. 
 Let's decode these changes one by one for you. 
 Five Big Changes From 1 November 2026 
 Delhi's Winter Pollution Control Measures 
 The most important right now is the Delhi pollution coming up soon. The winters in Delhi remain interesting for many reasons. The culturally rich national capital grabs lots of cultural attractions during winters. Also, Delhi is famous for its wholesale markets, and as the nation enters the wedding season, Delhi will become crowded. Crowds and pollution will be the peak problems in Delhi this coming winter. 
 Delhi's winter brings a thick layer of smog, making it really difficult to breathe and travel comfortably. 
 Now, to tackle all the above problems, authorities are expected to introduce stricter pollution-control measures from November 1. 
 The Delhi government, led by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, has announced a Permanent Winter Pollution Master Plan to tackle seasonal air pollution. The measures are scheduled to take effect from November 1, 2026, and will remain in force throughout the winter months to help curb pollution and improve air quality. 
 Delhi Winter Pollution Rules  
 Category 
 Key Change 
 Details 
 Vehicle Rules 
 Non-BS-VI Vehicle Ban 
 Certain non-BS-VI vehicles registered outside Delhi will reportedly be banned from November 1 to January 31. CNG, EVs and emergency services are exempt. 
   No PUCC, No Fuel 
 Vehicles without a valid PUCC will be denied fuel. 
   Double Parking Fees 
 Municipal parking charges will double from November 1 to February 28. DMRC parking is excluded. 
 Office Rules 
 50% Work From Home 
 Government and private offices will reportedly limit physical attendance to 50%, with essential-service exemptions. 
   Staggered Timings 
 MCD offices: 8:30 AM–5 PM; Delhi government offices: 10 AM–6:30 PM. 
 Construction Rules 
 Dust Control 
 Construction sites may face restrictions and require anti-smog guns and mist-suppression systems. 
   AI and Drone Monitoring 
 AI cameras and drones will reportedly monitor construction violations and open waste burning. 
   Winter Shutdown 
 A near-total construction and demolition ban is reportedly planned for December 10–January 20.

 Indian Railways' Advance Booking Window 
 If you are planning a winter vacation this semester-end or a trip home this season, you should definitely keep an eye on the updates. You should know about the rules changed by Indian Railways regarding advance booking. 
 The reported change in the Advance Reservation Period (ARP) from 120 days to 60 days could affect how passengers plan their journeys. 
 A shorter booking window may help curb speculative reservations and reduce cancellations made months before travel. 
 Before booking tickets for November or December, visit the official Indian Railways or IRCTC website for the latest updates. After all, a little planning goes a long way when securing a confirmed train ticket! 
 Indian Railways: New Train Ticket Booking Rules 
 Booking Window Reduced: The Advance Reservation Period (ARP) has been reduced from 120 days to 60 days, excluding the date of journey. 
 Exemptions: Certain daytime express trains, including the Taj Express and Gomti Express, retain shorter booking windows. The 365-day advance booking facility for foreign tourists remains unchanged. 
 Reason for Change: Around 21% of tickets booked 61–120 days in advance were reportedly cancelled, while another 4–5% resulted in no-shows. The shorter window aims to curb ticket hoarding and improve availability. 
 Aadhaar Verification: Aadhaar-authenticated users receive priority access to online general reserved ticket bookings on the first day of the reservation window. 
 Booking for Unverified Users: Users without Aadhaar verification must wait until the next day to book online after the reservation window opens.

 TRAI's Telecom Anti-Spam Measures 
 Your phone should connect you to people, not fraudsters. Keeping that in mind, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has been working on it as cybercrime has been increasing. 
 TRAI has made it mandatory to reflect caller ID when calling any other number. This step was taken to strengthen message traceability and curb spam, especially fraudulent messages impersonating banks and trusted organisations. 
 These measures aim to help telecom operators identify suspicious communications and reduce the risk of phishing. 
 It is also advised that users of Jio, Airtel, Vodafone Idea and BSNL should remain cautious about unfamiliar links and messages requesting personal or banking details. 
 TRAI has also warned users to never share OTPs, passwords or banking PINs. 
 TRAI's New Telecom Anti-Spam Rules:  
 1. AI-Based Spam Detection 
 AI Spam Filters: Telecom operators must use AI/ML tools to identify suspicious calling patterns and detect spam. 
 Link Whitelisting: URLs, APKs and OTT callback links in SMS templates must comply with applicable whitelisting requirements. 
 Number-Series Protection: The 1600 and 1601 series are designated for certain service and transactional calls, while the 140 series is used for promotional calls. 
 2. Blockchain and Spam Reporting 
 Spam Report Sharing: New rules reportedly require call-management platforms, including Truecaller, and smartphone manufacturers to share spam reports with telecom operators. 
 Blockchain Registry: Telecom operators use Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) to help track commercial communications and prevent spammers from evading detection by switching providers. 
 Truecaller's Concerns: Truecaller has reportedly raised concerns about data sharing and the potential competitive impact of the requirements. 
 3. Stricter Penalties for Spam 
 Automated Calls: Commercial automated messages and robocalls must comply with applicable registration and declaration requirements. 
 Repeat Complaints: Repeated spam complaints and network flags may trigger verification, suspension or disconnection, depending on the applicable rules. 
 Blacklisting: Violations involving commercial headers or communication rules can result in service suspension, restrictions on new resource allocations and industry blacklisting. 
 4. Caller ID (CNAP) Implementation 
 Verified Caller Names: Calling Name Presentation (CNAP) is being introduced to display the caller's KYC-registered name on compatible networks and devices. 
 Exemptions: Certain authorised government and intelligence users may qualify for caller identity restriction under applicable rules.

 Revised Banking and Credit Card Charges 
 Students and bank customers should keep an eye on their wallets because a big hit is coming their way. Several financial institutions are revising transaction fees, interest rates and reward limits. 
 Punjab National Bank (PNB) and ICICI Bank have announced changes reportedly taking effect in November. These changes could affect your day-to-day expenses and annual budget. 
 New Reserve Bank of India (RBI) nomination rules may also change how customers manage their bank accounts. 
 However, not every revision applies universally, as charges and conditions vary by bank and card type. Before making payments, customers should check official bank notifications and updated fee schedules.

 From November 1, 2026, cash advance fees increase to 2.5% or ₹400 (whichever is higher) at PNB ATMs and 2.5% or ₹500 at other domestic/overseas ATMs. Late payment fees for outstanding amounts above ₹10,000 are revised to ₹750.

 From November 15, finance charges apply to extended credit and cash advances. Monthly reward-point eligibility is capped for grocery, utility and insurance spends, depending on the card variant.

 Up to 3.75% per month, depending on the card variant 
 A 1% fee applies to rent payments, wallet loads exceeding ₹10,000 and utility payments exceeding ₹50,000, as stated in the provided details. 
 RBI's New Bank Nomination Rules 
 Feature 
 Details 
 Maximum number of nominees 
 Depositors can appoint up to four nominees for a savings account, locker or safe custody deposit. 
 Customised allocation 
 Account holders can specify percentage shares for nominees or establish an order of succession, subject to the applicable rules. 
 Key benefit 
 The changes aim to make the settlement of claims easier for surviving family members.

 Digital Life Certificate for Pensioners 
 The Digital Life Certificate, also known as Jeevan Pramaan, helps pensioners verify that they are alive and continue receiving their pension. Most eligible government pensioners must submit it annually in November. Digital submission options can make the process easier, while deadlines and requirements may vary by pension category. 
 Key Points to Know 
 General pensioners: The annual submission window is November 1–30, 2026, for eligible pensioners below 80 years. 
 Super-senior pensioners: Pensioners aged 80 years and above can submit their life certificates from October 1, 2026. 
 EPS-95 pensioners: Their life certificates generally remain valid for one year from the date of submission. 
 Smartphone face authentication: Eligible pensioners can use the AadhaarFaceRD and Jeevan Pramaan apps on a compatible Android smartphone to complete face authentication. 
 UMANG app: Pensioners can access Jeevan Pramaan services through the UMANG platform, subject to eligibility and authentication requirements. 
 Doorstep banking: Pensioners can request a home visit through eligible public sector bank doorstep banking services. 
 India Post Payments Bank (IPPB): Eligible pensioners can request doorstep assistance for biometric life certificate submission. 
 Documents and details required: Keep your Aadhaar number, mobile number, Pension Payment Order (PPO) number and pension bank account details ready. 
 Check eligibility: Pensioners should confirm the applicable submission process with their pension-disbursing bank or department, particularly if they are re-employed or remarried. 
 Avoid delays: Submit the certificate within the applicable deadline and confirm that it has been successfully recorded to help prevent pension payment disruptions.
